title: THE CALLED
mv: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
mvp: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.” 1 Peter 2:9
assignment: Mention five (5) attributes of the called (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: According to Scripture, “the called” refers to those whom God has chosen to fulfil His divine purpose (1 Peter 2:9). These are those summoned by God into a covenant relationship and are set apart for holiness, service, and eternal glory. The call of God is both a privilege and a responsibility. It is an invitation to respond to God’s love, who, in His sovereign mercy, draws people to Himself for salvation and service. It separates and equips individuals for holy living and positions them to fulfil God’s eternal agenda. To live a purposeful life, a Christian must understand his/her call.

God’s first call to humanity is the call to salvation through Jesus Christ (Matthew 11:28; Romans 10:9-11). This call brings one out of sin into the righteousness of Christ (2 Timothy 1:9). It is a call to be separated from worldliness to holy living, and those who answer it must live differently, reflecting God’s nature (2 Corinthians 6:17; 1 Peter 1:15-16). This call makes one serve God sincerely and bring others to Him (Matthew 4:19; John 15:16; Romans 1:1). It is also a call to suffer for Christ because the called are not exempt from trials (Philippians 1:29). The suffering, however, produces growth and eternal reward (Romans 8:17-18).
Ultimately, this call leads to eternal fellowship with Christ because the called are destined for an incorruptible inheritance in Him (Romans 8:30; 1 Peter 1:3-4).

From the Old Testament to the New Testament, we see men and women who were called by God-Abraham (Genesis 12:1-3), Moses (Exodus 3:4), Samuel (1 Samuel 3:4-10), Isaiah (Isaiah 6:8), Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:5-6), the disciples (Matthew 4:19), and Paul (Acts 9:3-6). All these people have common attributes, which are:

i: They heard God and responded to His call. Every believer must respond to the divine call (John 10:27).
They were chosen by God and separated wholly to Him. Being called involves divine election (Deuteronomy 7:6; 1 Peter 2:9).
They walked by faith, trusting God to the end. Believers must live by faith in God to the end (Hebrews 11:8; 2 Corinthians 5:7).
They demonstrated absolute obedience. Believers in Christ cannot do without obedience (Genesis 6:22; John 14:15).
They bore fruit. Those called in Christ are expected to manifest the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23) as well as the fruit of soul-winning (John 15:16).
They endured till the end. The called must persevere through trials and tribulations (Hebrews 10:36; Matthew 24:13).

b.x: Every believer must recognise that their call is not just an invitation but also a responsibility to walk in obedience, faith, and fruitfulness (Ephesians 4:1).
